advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the removed local `already_voted` pre-filter in reconcile is an acceptable per-poll Gerrit-call cost, or restore a cheap short-circuit that is safe under the new reset semantics.
evidence: Old code (diff): `if store.already_voted(change_id, revision): continue` — a cheap local skip before any network call.
New code src/rebar/review_bot/reconcile.py:263-265 unconditionally does `if await asyncio.to_thread(gc.has_llm_review_vote, change_id, revision): continue` for every candidate.
The removed docstring line said the local check was a deliberate `pre-filter here to avoid spawning needless reviews`.
reconcile.py:264 `if await asyncio.to_thread(gc.has_llm_review_vote, change_id, revision): continue`
voter.py:531 `if not force and await asyncio.to_thread(gc.has_llm_review_vote, change_id, revision):` runs again for the same change under the per-revision lock.
Test asserts this: test_review_bot.py `assert g.has_vote_calls == 2` with the comment 'Reconciler checks once, then the ordinary voter re-checks'.
advisory.finding: The reconciler removed the cheap local `store.already_voted(...)` pre-filter and now issues a Gerrit REST `has_llm_review_vote` call for EVERY candidate on EVERY reconcile pass (default every 300s), regardless of whether the change was already voted locally. On a repo with many open changes this converts a set of free SQLite lookups into N per-poll authenticated Gerrit reads.
merged_from: For each vote-less gap change the reconciler now performs the authoritative `has_llm_review_vote` read, and then the voter path (`review_and_vote`, force=False) performs `has_llm_review_vote` AGAIN under its lock (voter.py:531) — two Gerrit reads per reviewed gap change per pass.
scenarios: A backfill window containing many already-voted candidates now costs one Gerrit round-trip each per poll.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the added reset+verify round-trips on /rerun (new 502/409 failure paths) are the intended durability-vs-availability tradeoff for the operator escape hatch.
evidence: app.py:345 get_change_event, app.py:361 reset_llm_review_vote, app.py:372 has_llm_review_vote — three serial `asyncio.to_thread` Gerrit calls before the 202 at app.py:414.
Each has its own failure branch returning 502/409 (app.py:362-387).
advisory.finding: The `/rerun` operator endpoint now performs up to three sequential synchronous Gerrit round-trips (get_change_event, reset_llm_review_vote, has_llm_review_vote) before ACKing, each via asyncio.to_thread. This increases request latency and the number of independent Gerrit-failure points that turn a rerun into a 502/409 rather than an accepted enqueue.
scenarios: A transient Gerrit hiccup on the verification read now fails an operator rerun that previously would have enqueued.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify a real Gerrit label-reset comment-added event carries patchSet.revision AND patchSet.ref so `_candidate_events` admits it, otherwise the durable-recovery guarantee is unmet.
evidence: reconcile.py:179 `if not change_id or not patchset.get("revision") or not patchset.get("ref"): continue`
gerrit_client.py:228-229 docstring asserts the label write `emits a fresh patchset-bearing comment-added event, so reconciliation can recover the review`.
The only coverage (test_review_bot.py test_accepted_rerun_survives_restart_via_gerrit_reconcile) hand-constructs the reset event WITH `ref` set, so a missing-ref real event is untested.
advisory.finding: The durability claim relies on Gerrit's neutral-reset write emitting a patchset-bearing event that `_candidate_events` will accept, but that filter requires `patchSet.revision` AND `patchSet.ref` to be present on the emitted event; if the real `comment-added` label event omits `patchSet.ref`, the reset event is silently dropped as a candidate and the durability guarantee does not hold.
scenarios: If Gerrit's comment-added event for a label reset lacks patchSet.ref, reconcile drops it and the 'durable recovery' does not occur after queue loss.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests for retrigger.handle_comment_added GerritError paths: get_change_event raising and latest_bot_tag_state raising both yield RETRIGGER_REFUSED reason=eligibility-read-error and return None with no reset/enqueue.
evidence: retrigger.py:320 `except GerritError as exc:` around `fresh = gc.get_change_event(...)`
retrigger.py:346 `except GerritError as exc:` around `state = latest_bot_tag_state(...)`
search for 'eligibility-read-error' in tests/unit returned (no matches)
RetriggerGerrit.get_change_event / get_change_messages in test_review_bot_retrigger.py have no error-injection path (only reset_error/read_error on reset_llm_review_vote/has_llm_review_vote)
advisory.finding: The two new GerritError-handling branches in retrigger.handle_comment_added — a failure from gc.get_change_event (retrigger.py:318-329) and from latest_bot_tag_state (retrigger.py:344-356), both emitting RETRIGGER_REFUSED with reason='eligibility-read-error' and returning None — are not exercised by any test. The RetriggerGerrit double supports a reset/read error but never raises from get_change_event or get_change_messages, so a regression that (e.g.) crashed the worker instead of failing closed on an eligibility-read Gerrit error would go undetected.
scenarios: Gerrit returns a transient 5xx during current-revision lookup or change-message read on a recheck-review comment
A regression makes the eligibility-read failure crash the worker or fall through to acceptance instead of RETRIGGER_REFUSED
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend RetriggerGerrit to optionally raise GerritError from get_change_event and get_change_messages, and add two tests asserting result is None, reason 'eligibility-read-error' logged, gerrit.resets == [], and no forced event.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a client-level test where reset_llm_review_vote's _request returns a non-2xx status and assert it raises GerritError with the status attached.
evidence: search 'reset_llm_review_vote({change_id}) -> HTTP' in tests/unit returned (no matches)
advisory.finding: The new non-2xx branch of GerritClient.reset_llm_review_vote (raises GerritError when status is outside 200-299, gerrit_client.py:244-245) is untested. The only client-level test (test_reset_vote_body_is_fixed_neutral_and_ignores_contributor_text) stubs _request to return 200, and every higher-level fault test injects the GerritError at the test-double level rather than exercising the real status check. The contract that a failed HTTP status becomes a GerritError — which all downstream fail-closed refusals depend on — is never verified.
scenarios: Gerrit rejects the reset POST with a 403/409/5xx
A regression drops or inverts the status check so a failed reset is treated as success
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_reset_vote_body... or a sibling, set fake_request to return (503, ...) and assert pytest.raises(GerritError) with .status == 503.
